title: Transport of derived local Hom restriction to open subschemes
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $W\subseteq U$ opens with inclusion $i$, and fix derived categories in morphism universe $w$ for module sheaves on $X,U,W$ and on the localized sites over $U,W$ [def-pc-derived-category]. Let $r_T$ denote overFunctor and $e_T$ the exact open-site equivalence overEquiv. Put $R_T=D(r_Te_T)$, $S=D(e_U^{-1}\operatorname{overMap}(i)e_W)$, let $\alpha:R_US\cong R_W$ be the canonical comparison induced by the unit of $e_U$ and overFunctorMap, and let $q_T:R_T\cong D(r_T)D(e_T)$ be mapDerivedCategoryCompIso. For $F,E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ and $a:R_UF\to R_UE$, put $a_0=D(e_U)^{-1}(q_U(F)^{-1}a q_U(E))$, using the full-faithful preimage on Hom. Then $\alpha(F)^{-1}S(a)\alpha(E)=q_W(F)D(e_W)(\operatorname{derivedOpenHomRestriction}(X,i,a_0))q_W(E)^{-1}$ [lem-sc-derived-hom-mayer-vietoris]. Products in this formula follow Lean composition order from left to right.

proof.text: Prove the composition-comparison component formulas on Q(K) from Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso_fac: the complex-level comparison for the composite is the identity, as checked degreewise. Cancel the factorization isomorphisms to solve for both hom and inv. Similarly solve Functor.mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_fac for the derived natural-isomorphism component. These are the proved private helpers comp_fac, comp_hom_Q, comp_inv_Q, and nat_hom_Q.

For exact functors A:C→D, e:D→E, S:E→I, T:D→H, v:H→I, B:C→H, and isomorphisms κ:eS≅Tv and γ:AT≅B, form α by pasting κ and γ with associators. Put k=q(e,S)⁻¹ D(κ) q(T,v) and d=q(A,T)⁻¹ D(γ). Prove q(Ae,S)⁻¹ D(α) q(B,v) = (q(A,e) whiskered with D(S)) (D(A) whiskered with k) (d whiskered with D(v)). Apply Localization.natTrans_ext along DerivedCategory.Q. Use the preceding component formulas. Move k across A.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.inv by naturality; expand k and d at Q(K) and cancel the factorization inverse pairs. Naturality of v.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.inv moves the remaining γ component into Q. The resulting equality of complex morphisms follows degreewise from the definition of α and the identity associators. This is the fully proved private helper pasting.

Prove the general morphism transport formula (private helper transport). For b=D(e).preimage(q(A,e)⁻¹ a q(A,e)), use Functor.map_preimage to obtain D(e)(b)=q(A,e)⁻¹ a q(A,e). Evaluate the pasted-square identity at F and E. Precompose the desired equality with the forward α-derived comparison at F and postcompose with q(B,v) at E. Rewrite both sides with the square identity, cancel d(F) with its inverse, rewrite a q(A,e)(E)=q(A,e)(F)D(e)(b), and apply the naturality equation of k to b. Canceling the outer isomorphisms yields the required conjugation. Only fullness of D(e) is needed; all helpers are proved without sorry.

Specialize A and B to overFunctor at U and W, T to overMap(i), e and v to the open-site equivalence functors at U and W, and S to e_U.inverse⋙T⋙v. Take κ to be the associator, the inverse unit of overEquiv U whiskered with T⋙v, and the left unitor; take γ=overFunctorMap(i). Fullness of D(e) follows from the existing derived-equivalence instance. The pasted α-derived comparison is definitionally the eU in the statement, and d⁻¹D(T)(b)d is definitionally derivedOpenHomRestriction. Apply transport directly. No Mayer–Vietoris exactness theorem is used, and no covering or nonemptiness assumption occurs.

theorem scheme_derived_hom_restriction_transport
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (U W : X.Opens) (i : W ⟶ U)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings W.toScheme.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over W))]
    (F E : schemeDerivedCategory X) :
    let R_U := (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U ⋙
          Equivalence.functor
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U)).mapDerivedCategory
    let S_U := (Equivalence.inverse
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U) ⋙
          SheafOfModules.overMap.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) i ⋙
          Equivalence.functor
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over W))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings W.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv W)).mapDerivedCategory
    let eU := ((Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso
          (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U ⋙
          Equivalence.functor
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U))
          (Equivalence.inverse
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U) ⋙
          SheafOfModules.overMap.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) i ⋙
          Equivalence.functor
            (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over W))
            (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings W.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
            (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv W))).symm ≪≫
        Functor.mapDerivedCategoryNatIso
          (Functor.associator _ _ _ ≪≫
          Functor.isoWhiskerLeft
            (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U)
            ((Functor.associator _ _ _).symm ≪≫
              Functor.isoWhiskerRight (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U).unitIso.symm _ ≪≫
                Functor.leftUnitor _) ≪≫
          (Functor.associator _ _ _).symm ≪≫
          Functor.isoWhiskerRight
            (SheafOfModules.overFunctorMap.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) i)
            (Equivalence.functor
              (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over W))
              (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings W.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
              (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv W))))
    let e := Equivalence.functor
      (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
      (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
      (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U)
    let eW := Equivalence.functor
      (C := SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over W))
      (D := SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings W.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
      (Scheme.Modules.overEquiv W)
    let qU := Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso
      (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U) e
    let qW := Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso
      (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) W) eW
    ∀ (a : R_U.obj F ⟶ R_U.obj E),
      eU.inv.app F ≫ S_U.map a ≫ eU.hom.app E =
        qW.hom.app F ≫ eW.mapDerivedCategory.map
          (derivedOpenHomRestriction X.toRingedSpace i
            (e.mapDerivedCategory.preimage (qU.inv.app F ≫ a ≫ qU.hom.app E))) ≫
          qW.inv.app E
